agency: Any mayoral agency under the jurisdiction of the DCAS commissioner (the Clerical Associate list used by mayoral agencies; NYC Health + Hospitals has a separate title and list)
union: District Council 37, AFSCME (Clerical-Administrative bargaining unit; Local 1549 describes itself as representing Clerical Associates)
title_code_or_exam: Clerical Associate, title code 10251, competitive class, open-competitive. Latest exam: New York City Bridge Exam No. 5977 (filing June 4-24, 2025). Latest dated open-competitive list: Exam No. 3120 (established April 30, 2025)

hiring.summary: A Clerical Associate gets a permanent job by passing a DCAS civil service exam, landing on a ranked eligible list and being picked by an agency from among the top three available names. After a one-year probation the job is permanent. When no list is available, agencies can hire provisionally without a competitive test, but only until a list arrives.

nodes.title: Exam is announced and the candidate applies online
nodes.body: The Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) posts a notice of examination; the candidate files on the Online Application System (OASys) and pays a $47 fee, which is waived for veterans, unemployed people and people receiving public assistance or Supplemental Security Income. clerical associate requires a high school diploma or equivalent and one year of full-time clerical experience.
nodes.time: Filing window of at least 2 weeks; 20 days for the 2025 exam (June 4 to June 24)
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 50(5); Personnel Rule 4.2.2; Notice of Examination No. 5977

nodes.title: Candidate takes the test
nodes.body: In 2025 clerical associate was part of the New York City Bridge Exam: a computer-based multiple-choice test that sets list rank (70% needed to pass), a pass/fail education and experience review and a typing test of 20 words per minute. The 2021 clerical associate exam was scored only on education and experience.
nodes.time: Testing began Sept. 15, 2025, about 12 weeks after filing closed
nodes.law: Notice of Examination No. 5977; Notice of Examination No. 1190 (2021)

nodes.title: Scores are finalized and an eligible list is established
nodes.body: Passing candidates are ranked by final score. Veterans who claim credit get 5 extra points (10 if disabled), added only when the list is established. The list becomes official by order of the DCAS commissioner.
nodes.time: Median 163 days from exam to results for all DCAS exams (July to October 2024)

nodes.title: The list stays alive for up to four years
nodes.body: State law sets a list's life at one to four years; DCAS says City lists typically last four. The most recent open-competitive clerical associate list with a posted date (Exam No. 3120) was established April 30, 2025 and runs to April 30, 2029.

nodes.question: When an agency fills a funded vacancy, is an appropriate eligible list available?

nodes.title: DCAS certifies the top names to the agency
nodes.body: The agency must pick one of the three highest-ranked candidates who are willing to accept the job.
nodes.time: When the agency requests a certification

nodes.title: Agency interviews and makes an offer
nodes.body: At the appointment interview the agency verifies qualifications and, where required, New York City residency within 90 days of appointment. A candidate who declines or does not answer an offer in the time the agency sets can be withheld from further certification.
nodes.time: At least 4 days to respond to an offer
nodes.law: Personnel Rule 4.8.2; Administrative Code § 12-120 (as described in the exam notice)

nodes.title: Character and background review
nodes.body: Satisfactory character and reputation is a minimum qualification. DCAS can investigate after appointment and revoke the appointment for disqualifying facts or fraud.
nodes.time: Revocation possible up to 3 years after appointment

nodes.title: Appointment and probation
nodes.body: The new clerical associate serves a probationary term. The default for competitive-class appointments is one year. It can be extended by up to six months with the employee's written consent and is extended by days spent on leave or limited duty.

nodes.title: Permanent status
nodes.body: After probation the employee holds a permanent competitive-class appointment and can be disciplined only for cause after charges and a hearing under Civil Service Law § 75, or through the District Council 37 contract procedure.

nodes.title: Agency nominates a provisional hire
nodes.body: With no usable list, the agency can nominate someone. DCAS reviews the nominee's training and experience, without a written test, and the person is appointed provisionally. Provisional employees in the title can file late for the next exam in some cases.

nodes.title: Provisional job ends when a list arrives
nodes.body: A provisional appointment must end within two months after an appropriate list is established. To stay, the person has to be reached on the list and appointed permanently.

end_to_end.text: No official source gives a start-to-finish figure. Adding the official clocks for the 2025 exam: about 12 weeks from the close of filing to the test, a median of 163 days for DCAS to produce results (all DCAS exams, July to October 2024), an open-ended wait to be reached on a list that can last four years, then a 12-month probation. Even a candidate hired the day results come out would reach permanent status about 20 months after filing closed.

firing.summary: How a Clerical Associate can be fired depends on status. A probationer can be let go without a hearing after two months of service. A provisional employee has contract protection only after two years. A permanent employee can be removed only for incompetency or misconduct after written charges, and after a Step A conference chooses between a Section 75 hearing at OATH, with appeal to the Civil Service Commission or court, and the union contract route ending in binding arbitration.

nodes.question: What is the employee's civil service status?

nodes.title: Agency can end employment without a hearing
nodes.body: After a minimum of two months of service, the agency head can terminate a probationer whose conduct and performance are not satisfactory, by notice to the employee and to DCAS. At the end of probation, an unsatisfactory probationer can be let go the same way. The contract's disciplinary procedure covers permanent employees, not probationers.
nodes.time: Any time from month 2 to the end of probation
nodes.law: Personnel Rules 5.2.7(a), 5.2.7(c); Clerical Agreement Article VI § 1(e)

nodes.title: Terminated probationer may go back on the list
nodes.body: DCAS has discretion to restore the person's name to the eligible list if it still exists.

nodes.title: Investigatory interview
nodes.body: An employee questioned as a potential subject of discipline has a right to union representation and must be told of it in writing beforehand. Under the DC 37 contract, when the interviewer is outside the normal chain of command, the employee may bring a union representative or lawyer.
nodes.time: Written notice at least 2 work days ahead, when feasible
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 75(2); 2017-2021 DC 37 Memorandum of Agreement, Article IX § 19

nodes.title: Agency serves written charges
nodes.body: Charges must allege incompetency or misconduct and be filed within 18 months of the conduct, unless it would be a crime. The employee gets at least eight days to answer in writing and can be suspended without pay for up to 30 days while charges are pending.
nodes.time: Within 18 months of the conduct; 8 days to answer; suspension capped at 30 days

nodes.title: Step A conference
nodes.body: An agency designee meets with the employee, who may bring a union representative, and issues a written determination. The employee can accept it, signing away Section 75 and 76 rights, or reject it.
nodes.time: Decision by the end of the 5th day after the conference
nodes.law: Clerical Agreement Article VI § 5, Step A

nodes.question: If the employee rejects Step A, which track?

nodes.title: Hearing at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
nodes.body: By default the agency proceeds under Section 75. The Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) hears City cases; an administrative law judge first holds a settlement conference, and unsettled cases go to trial before a different judge. The agency must prove its case by a preponderance of the evidence, and the employee may have counsel or a union representative.
nodes.time: OATH averaged 26.5 days from close of record to decision (July to October 2024)
nodes.who: Agency lawyers; employee; union or counsel; OATH judge
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 75(2); NYC Charter § 1048; Clerical Agreement Article VI § 5, Step B(i)

nodes.title: Agency head decides
nodes.body: The judge's report and recommendation go to the agency head, who makes the final decision. Penalties range from a reprimand or a fine of up to $100 to suspension of up to two months, demotion or dismissal.

nodes.title: Appeal
nodes.body: The employee can appeal to the New York City Civil Service Commission or go to state court under Article 78 of the Civil Practice Law and Rules.
nodes.time: Commission appeal within 20 days of notice (23 if notice is mailed by registered mail)
nodes.who: Employee; Civil Service Commission or state Supreme Court

nodes.title: Step B: appeal to the agency head
nodes.body: The union, with the employee's consent, elects the contract route, and both file a written waiver of Section 75 and 76 rights. Unpaid suspension still cannot exceed 30 days. The agency head or a designee meets with them and can impose discipline up to termination.
nodes.time: File within 5 work days; decision by the 10th work day
nodes.law: Clerical Agreement Article VI § 5, Steps B(i)-(ii)

nodes.title: Step C: appeal to the Commissioner of Labor Relations
nodes.body: Either the employee or the union can appeal to the City's labor relations commissioner. If the penalty is termination or more than 30 days of unpaid suspension, the union can skip this step. If the City misses a deadline, the next step can be invoked.
nodes.time: File within 10 days; reply within 15 work days
nodes.who: Union; employee; Office of Labor Relations

nodes.title: Step D: arbitration
nodes.body: Only the union, with the employee's consent, can take the case to a neutral arbitrator under the Office of Collective Bargaining. The award is final and binding, and the two sides split the cost. Small penalties (a fine of one week's pay or less, or a written reprimand) can go to expedited arbitration.
nodes.time: Union files within 15 work days of the prior determination
nodes.law: Clerical Agreement Article VI §§ 2-3 (Step IV), 5 (Step D), 16; 61 RCNY

aside.label: Provisional employees
aside.text: Section 75 covers permanent competitive-class employees, not provisionals. Under the contract, a provisional employee of a mayoral agency can grieve discipline only after two years of unbroken service in the same or similar title, under a separate 2011 and 2018 procedure.

stats.text: DCAS median time from exam administration to exam results: 163 days in the first four months of fiscal 2025 (July to October 2024), across all DCAS-administered exams. The agency target is 197 days.

OATH's Trials Division, which hears City employee discipline cases among many other case types, received 897 cases of all types in the first four months of fiscal 2025 and averaged 26.5 days from close of record to decision.
OATH says agency heads adopted 99% of its Trials Division findings in 2016.

The open-competitive clerical associate list from Exam No. 3120 was established April 30, 2025 and expires April 30, 2029; the active-list dataset showed 2,653 names on it as of Sept. 11, 2026. A later clerical associate list (Exam No. 4129) was published Nov. 26, 2025, with no establishment date in the dataset.

The Preliminary Mayor's Management Report for fiscal 2025 says the last round of qualified incumbent exams, part of DCAS's provisional reduction plan, ran in the first four months of fiscal 2024, and that the City is now in compliance with Civil Service Law § 65.

caveats: Title choice: Clerical Associate (title code 10251) was chosen because it is a competitive-class, open-competitive title listed in Article I of the District Council 37 Clerical Agreement and was tested as recently as the 2025 Bridge Exam. The 'largest DC 37 local' framing for Local 1549 is not confirmed by an official source.

Contract currency: the most recent full Clerical unit agreement posted by the Office of Labor Relations runs March 3, 2010 to Sept. 25, 2017. Its terms are carried forward by § 11 of the 2017-2021 DC 37 memorandum and § 16 of the 2021-2026 DC 37 memorandum, which only changes economic terms. That memorandum's term ends Nov. 6, 2026, so the procedure could change in the next round. No successor unit agreement was found on the OLR site.
Contract quotes come from the PDF's scanned text layer; obvious OCR errors were corrected in the quotes (for example 'hy' to 'by', 'live' to 'five', '75( I)' to '75(1)').

The Clerical Agreement's disciplinary procedure (Article VI § 5) has Steps A, B, C and D. It has no separate 'OATH conference' step; in this summary, the OATH settlement conference falls inside the statutory Section 75 track, per OATH's own description of its practice.

Probation length: the 2025 notice states an 18-month probation only for Child Protective Specialist (source 33) and gives none for Clerical Associate, so the one-year default in Personnel Rule 5.2.1 is shown. That is an inference from the rule, not a title-specific statement.
The minimum service before a probationer can be terminated mid-probation is two months for an original appointment (Personnel Rule 5.2.7(c)), not two weeks.

The 163-day median covers all DCAS-administered exams and measures time to 'exam results completion', which may not equal the date a list is formally established. The 20-month figure in end_to_end adds official clocks together; it is not a measured figure.

Exam format changes over time: the 2021 Clerical Associate exam (No. 1190) was scored on education and experience alone with a $40 fee, and the 2025 Bridge Exam added a multiple-choice test and a $47 fee. The fiscal 2026 Bridge Exam (No. 6977) schedule does not list Clerical Associate.
OATH statistics cover all Trials Division case types, not only employee discipline, and none are specific to DC 37 or Clerical Associates.
The New York City residency requirement is described from the exam notice's summary of Administrative Code § 12-120; the Code itself was not fetched.
Civil Service Law text comes from the NewYork.Public.Law mirror (which cites nysenate.gov, verified Sept. 5, 2026) because nysenate.gov served a bot-check page to every request.
unverified: Application and test dates for Clerical Associate Exam No. 3120 and Exam No. 4129: the notices were not found at nyc.gov (404) or in the Wayback Machine, so exam-to-list time for Clerical Associate specifically could not be calculated.
Whether a Clerical Associate list from Exam No. 5977 has been established: the Open Data API returned 'service unavailable' or no rows for that exam number.

Current provisional headcount: counts of 23,052 (February 2016) and about 16,821 (December 2018) appeared only in search snippets of DCAS progress reports and were not confirmed from a fetched document.

Text of the 'Disciplinary Procedure for Provisional Employees' (DC 37 agreements of Aug. 30, 2011 and April 27, 2018): Article VI § 6 of the contract refers to it, but the text was not in the posted PDF and was not found separately.
NYC Civil Service Commission disciplinary-appeal page (nyc.gov/site/csc/appeals/disciplinary-appeals.page) returned 404; the appeal procedure is sourced to Civil Service Law § 76 only.
OATH rules of practice (48 RCNY) and Office of Collective Bargaining arbitration rules (61 RCNY) were not fetched, so no rule-level clocks for OATH conferences or arbitration scheduling are given.
Local 1549 as the 'largest' DC 37 local: not confirmed from an official or union source that was fetched.
Legacy credit (named in the exam notice) was not researched.
